- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon; apply a 1–2% upward bias for early period.  
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction in next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.5), model fails to adjust quickly; apply mean reversion bias toward 3–5 day average of recent 10–15 prices.  
- Model tends to ignore sentiment volatility in early forecast days; if sentiment swings sharply, apply lag correction: delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment changes >0.5.
